text:
Sometimes they are clear, and sometimes wheat-colored

like earth burned by the sun's fire...

The Creole woman whose lips carry a faint flush

and whose dark eyes carry a dreaming soul...


When the strings of a sad guitar weep,

her eyes are dyed the color of illusion,

and from her warm breast her heart departs,

when the strings of a sad guitar weep...


In the pale hours of moonlit nights,

beneath the discreet canopy of the shadowy amate,

her eyes reflect like the ripples of a river

in the pale hours of moonlit nights...


When she goes on Sundays to the nearby church,

with her dark, olive-colored eyes,

compliments follow her and love importunes her,

when she goes on Sundays to the nearby church...


When the strings of a sweet guitar weep,

in the pale hours of moonlit nights,

her olive-colored eyes grow sad,

when the strings of a sweet guitar weep.

translation.title: The Creole Woman's Eyes
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem’s refrain structure and its local images of the amate tree, olive-colored eyes, and guitars.
